prompt: One CPU, strict priorities: H highest, then M, then L. No priority inheritance. Measure milliseconds after L locks `m`. At the starting instant L locks `m`; its critical section needs 3 ms of CPU. After 1 millisecond H wakes and blocks on `m`. After 2 milliseconds M becomes runnable and needs 100 ms of CPU, using no locks. When does H acquire `m`? And when would it with priority inheritance?

options.text: 103 ms without inheritance; 3 ms with it
options.explanation: Correct. Without inheritance M preempts L from 2 to 102 ms, and L finishes its last 1 ms at 103. With inheritance L runs at H's priority after 1 millisecond, M cannot preempt, and L unlocks at 3 ms.
Without inheritance L has only priority L, so M (which outranks it) preempts it after 2 milliseconds and runs for 100 ms before L can continue.

options.text: 102 ms without inheritance; 2 ms with it
options.explanation: This forgets the critical section's remaining work. After 2 milliseconds L has done 2 of its 3 ms, so it still needs 1 ms after M stops.

options.text: Never without inheritance, because H is deadlocked
options.explanation: There's no cycle. M finishes after 100 ms, then L runs and releases `m`. The delay is unbounded in general (more M-level work could arrive), but here it ends.

workedExample:
Without inheritance:

```
0-1    L runs (1 ms of CS done)
1      H wakes, blocks on m
1-2    L runs (2 ms done)
2-102  M runs (preempts L)
102-103 L runs (3 ms), unlocks
103    H acquires m
```

With inheritance:

```
0-1    L runs (1 ms done)
1      H blocks; L inherits H
1-3    L runs (3 ms done); M can't
       preempt after 2 ms
3      L unlocks, drops back to L;
       H acquires m
```

H's wait is the time it acquires `m` minus the time it blocked:

```formula
w = t_acq − t_block
w_none = 103 ms − 1 ms = 102 ms
w_PI = 3 ms − 1 ms = 2 ms
where
t_block: when H blocked on m: 1 ms
t_acq: when H acquires m
w: how long H waits
w_none: H's wait without priority inheritance
w_PI: H's wait with priority inheritance (PI)
ms: milliseconds
In words: inheritance cuts H's wait from 102 ms to the 2 ms L still needed in its critical section.
```

Without inheritance the wait is unbounded in general, since any M-level work extends it; with inheritance it is bounded by L's remaining critical-section work in this stated three-task, single-CPU model.
